core_finding: The Warriors selection failed. The recorded 60% was only 0.97 percentage points above the latest normalized market baseline of 59.03%, so the principal defect was not a market-uplift breach. The pre-match record already contained a strong Dolphins counter-case: seven consecutive wins, a 26-24 Round 17 win over the Warriors, restored Cobbo/Nikorima/Finefeuiaki combinations, and role-critical attacking evidence through Katoa, Nikorima and Tabuai-Fidow. MAYHEM reduced the Warriors from 62% to 60% after the prior failure audit, but still allowed the Warriors season differential, home-final record and structural strength to dominate the final directional decision. The process correction is to require an explicit team-level synthesis when current-form, restored-unit continuity, matchup evidence and role-critical production all support the opposing case simultaneously.

pre_match_evidence.market: Warriors $1.61 / Dolphins $2.32; overround-adjusted Warriors 59.03% / Dolphins 40.97%; MAYHEM Warriors 60%, delta +0.97pp. Market gate CLEAR.
pre_match_evidence.structural_baseline: Warriors approximately +310 season point differential versus Dolphins approximately +156; Warriors six straight wins and eight of 10 at Go Media Stadium; Dolphins seven straight wins.
pre_match_evidence.roster: Warriors had Leka Halasima, Wayde Egan and Kurt Capewell returning with Jackson Ford on the interchange. Dolphins restored Selwyn Cobbo, Kodi Nikorima and Kulikefu Finefeuiaki.
pre_match_evidence.player_statistics: Role-critical pre-match profiles included Isaiya Katoa with 17 try assists and about 482 average kicking metres, Kodi Nikorima with 16 try assists and 23 line-break assists, and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow with 13 tries, 77 tackle breaks and about 184 average running metres.
pre_match_evidence.matchup: Dolphins had beaten Warriors 26-24 in Round 17; the season series was split and recent meetings were structurally competitive.
pre_match_evidence.weather: Windy Auckland conditions were retained as execution variance only, with no demonstrated directional team edge.
pre_match_evidence.counter_case: Dolphins current form, restored unit continuity, prior win and role-critical attacking production formed a coherent evidence-supported upset mechanism.
pre_match_evidence.checkpoint_integrity: T-24h, T-3h and T-60m were captured before kickoff. T-10 was MISSED_NOT_CAPTURED and remains immutable.

tests.confidence_inflation: NOT_FOUND: +0.97pp versus normalized market was inside the +3pp gate.
tests.correlated_evidence_stacking: NO MATERIAL DEFECT IDENTIFIED in the recorded market/structural evidence families.
tests.structural_baseline_suppression: PARTIAL IN REVERSE: Warriors season differential and venue strength were valid but retained too much directional dominance once the Dolphins opposing evidence converged.
tests.roster_role_underweighting: FOUND: the restored Dolphins combination was recognized but not translated strongly enough at team level.
tests.player_statistical_underweighting: FOUND: role-critical Dolphins production was captured but did not materially alter the preferred selection beyond the 62% to 60% reduction.
tests.narrative_dominance: FOUND: Warriors structural/home narrative remained preferred despite multiple independent opposing football mechanisms.

result_sources: News.com.au reported the Dolphins victory and the late sequence from 20-16 to Jack Bostock sealing the result.
Courier-Mail reported the final score as Dolphins 26-16 Warriors.
verified_events: Dolphins won 26-16 after trailing 16-8 around the hour mark.
Herbie Farnworth scored to narrow the deficit.
Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow broke away in the decisive comeback passage.
Jack Bostock scored the late sealing try.
Tom Flegler left after a concussion during the match.
post_match_validation.causal_separation: Flegler's concussion, sin-bins and all other in-match events are post-kickoff evidence and are excluded from the pre-match failure finding. The audit defect is limited to pre-kickoff synthesis of current form, restored combinations, matchup evidence and player production.

confidence_error.finding: No excess-confidence gate breach occurred. The error was directional synthesis rather than unsupported market uplift.

failure_mechanisms.finding: The Dolphins counter-case was explicit and multi-source but did not produce a sufficient directional reassessment.
Cobbo, Nikorima and Finefeuiaki were assessed as a restored combination, but its team-level effect remained underweighted.
Katoa, Nikorima and Tabuai-Fidow production was captured yet did not sufficiently affect the final team comparison.
Warriors season differential and home record retained too much influence after the opposing evidence converged.
T-10 was MISSED_NOT_CAPTURED. This does not alter the INCORRECT grade but removed the final mandatory validation opportunity.

mandatory_corrections: CONVERGENT_OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_GATE: when current form, restored-unit continuity, relevant matchup evidence and role-critical player production all support the opposing side, require an explicit switch-or-reduce test before retaining the preferred team.
TEAM_LEVEL_COMBINATION_SYNTHESIS: translate multiple restored role-critical players into a team mechanism rather than preserving them as parallel notes.
PLAYER_STAT_DECISION_EFFECT: role-critical statistical comparisons must state whether they strengthen, weaken or leave unchanged the team-level selection and why.
STRUCTURAL_BASELINE_BALANCE: strong season differential and venue history cannot by themselves override convergent current opposing evidence.
T10_INTEGRITY: retain MISSED_NOT_CAPTURED permanently; no reconstruction.
PUBLIC_GRADE_SEPARATION: Warriors 60% remains the genuine historical selection and is publicly graded INCORRECT without calibration qualifiers.
information_advantage: NONE: the result alone does not demonstrate an information advantage.
integrity: No retrospective tip switch, no probability rewrite, and no use of post-kickoff events as pre-match evidence.
